start.title: In the Beginning
start.text:
You are God — Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
Nothing has been created yet. What is your first act?

choices.text: Remain silent and alone forever
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:1, God's first act was to create the heavens and the earth.

choices.text: Create the heavens and the earth
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:1: 'In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.'

choices.text: Speak only to yourself
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:1, God did not stay silent — He created the heavens and the earth.

silence.title: The Formless Earth
silence.text:
The earth is formless and void.
Darkness covers the deep. What do you do?

choices.text: Say: 'Let there be light'
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:3: 'And God said, Let there be light.'

choices.text: Command more darkness to cover everything
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:3, God said 'Let there be light' — not more darkness.

voice.title: The Spirit Over the Waters
voice.text:
The Spirit of God hovers over the waters.
What do you speak into being first?

choices.text: 'Let there be light'
choices.feedback: light was the first thing God spoke into being (Genesis 1:3).

choices.text: 'Let there be trees and animals'
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1, God created light first — plants come on Day Three, animals on Days Five and Six.

void.title: The Deep
void.text:
The earth is without form; darkness covers the deep.
The Spirit of God hovers over the waters. What now?

choices.text: Say: 'Let there be light'
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:3: 'Let there be light.'

choices.text: Create humans right away
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1, humans are created on the sixth day, not first. Light comes first.

light.title: Light Has Come
light.text:
Light shines. You see that the light is good.
What is your next act on Day One?

choices.text: Add a second sun in the sky
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:4, God separated the light from the darkness — He did not create a second sun.

choices.text: Erase the darkness completely
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:4-5, God did not destroy darkness — He separated it from light and named it Night.

choices.text: Separate the light from the darkness
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:4: 'And God separated the light from the darkness.'

light_obey.title: Day and Night
light_obey.text:
Light shines and it is good.
How do you complete the first day?

choices.text: Call the light Day and the darkness Night
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:5: 'God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night.'

choices.text: Create the sun, moon, and stars now
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1, the sun, moon, and stars are created on the fourth day — not the first.

light_awe.title: The First Day
light_awe.text:
There is light. There is darkness.
What completes the first day?

choices.text: Make the sea creatures now
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:20-23, sea creatures come on Day Five. Day One separates light and darkness.

choices.text: Call the light Day and the darkness Night
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:5: God called the light Day and the darkness Night.

warmth.title: The Second Day
warmth.text:
The first day is complete.
What do you create on Day Two?

choices.text: An expanse to separate the waters above from below
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:6-7: God made an expanse and separated the waters above from the waters below.

choices.text: Plant the first garden
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:11, plants come on Day Three. Day Two is the expanse — the sky.

day_night.title: The Second Day
day_night.text:
Evening and morning — the first day is done.
What comes on Day Two?

choices.text: Create the expanse and call it Heaven
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:8: 'And God called the expanse Heaven.'

choices.text: Create fish and birds
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:20-23, fish and birds come on Day Five — not Day Two.

sky.title: The Third Day
sky.text:
The expanse of Heaven is made.
What is your first act on Day Three?

choices.text: Command dry land to appear without moving the waters
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:9, God first gathered the waters together — then the dry land appeared.

choices.text: Gather the waters together into one place
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:9: 'Let the waters be gathered into one place, and let the dry land appear.'

choices.text: Create the sun to warm the sky
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:14-16, the sun is made on the fourth day — not the third.

sky_vast.title: The Third Day
sky_vast.text:
The expanse of Heaven is complete.
What comes on Day Three?

choices.text: Create the stars first
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:14-16, stars are created on the fourth day. Day Three is dry land and seas.

choices.text: Gather the waters into seas so dry land appears
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:9-10: God gathered the waters into seas and dry land appeared.

waters_gather.title: Dry Land Appears
waters_gather.text:
The waters gather. Dry land emerges.
What do you do next on Day Three?

choices.text: Cover the land with plants, seeds, and fruit trees
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:11: 'Let the earth sprout vegetation, plants yielding seed, and fruit trees.'

choices.text: Fill the seas with fish right now
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:20-21, fish come on Day Five. Day Three ends with plants and trees.

expanse.title: The Third Day
expanse.text:
The heavens stretch above.
What do you do on Day Three?

choices.text: Bring forth dry land, plants, and fruit trees
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:9-12: dry land, seas, and vegetation appear on Day Three.

choices.text: Form Adam from the dust
choices.feedback: In Genesis 2:7, Adam is formed on Day Six — not Day Three.

land.title: Vegetation
land.text:
Dry land appears.
What kind of life do you cover it with?

choices.text: Plants, herbs, and fruit trees — each according to its kind
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:11-12: plants and trees each 'according to its kind.'

choices.text: Only flowers, and no trees
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:11, God made plants, herbs, AND fruit trees — not flowers alone.

choices.text: Wild animals to roam the mountains
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:24-25, land animals come on the sixth day — not the third.

land_emerge.title: The Earth Brings Forth
land_emerge.text:
The dry ground is ready.
What sprouts on Day Three?

choices.text: Vegetation with seed, and fruit trees bearing fruit
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:11: 'plants yielding seed, and fruit trees bearing fruit... each according to its kind.'

choices.text: Bees and butterflies before any plants
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:24-25, creeping things come on Day Six. Day Three brings plants first.

plants.title: The Fourth Day
plants.text:
Day Three is complete — plants and trees cover the earth.
What do you create on Day Four?

choices.text: Lights in the expanse — sun, moon, and stars
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:14-16: God made the sun, moon, and stars on Day Four.

choices.text: Sea creatures and birds
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:20-23, sea creatures and birds come on Day Five — not Day Four.

flowers.title: The Fourth Day
flowers.text:
Plants cover the earth.
What comes on Day Four?

choices.text: Adam and Eve
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:26-27, humans are created on Day Six — not Day Four.

choices.text: The sun, moon, and stars
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:14-19: God set the sun, moon, and stars in the expanse of the heavens.

mountain.title: The Fourth Day
mountain.text:
The land is full of plants and trees.
What do you make on Day Four?

choices.text: Sun, moon, and stars in the heavens
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:14-19: God set two great lights and the stars in the expanse of the heavens.

choices.text: Rain, snow, and clouds
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1, Day Four is about the sun, moon, and stars — not weather.

stars.title: The Greater and Lesser Lights
stars.text:
Lights are set in the heavens.
How do you order them?

choices.text: One single light to rule both day and night
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:16, God made TWO great lights — the greater for the day and the lesser for the night.

choices.text: Only stars — no sun, no moon
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:16, God made the sun and the moon as well as the stars.

choices.text: A greater light to rule the day, a lesser to rule the night, and the stars
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:16: 'The greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night — and the stars.'

stars_delight.title: Lights in the Heavens
stars_delight.text:
Day Four continues.
What is set in place?

choices.text: The sun, the moon, and countless stars
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:14-16: sun, moon, and stars — for signs and seasons, days and years.

choices.text: Just one small light for the whole sky
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:16, God made TWO great lights, plus the stars — not one small light.

stars_vision.title: Stars Beyond Number
stars_vision.text:
You place lights in the heavens.
How many stars will there be?

choices.text: Countless — beyond number
choices.feedback: Genesis 15:5 and 22:17 describe the stars of heaven as too many to count.

choices.text: Exactly seven stars — no more
choices.feedback: In Scripture, God's stars are innumerable — 'as the stars of the sky in multitude' (Genesis 22:17).

countless_stars.title: The Fifth Day
countless_stars.text:
The lights of Day Four are set.
What do you create on Day Five?

choices.text: Creatures that swarm the waters, and birds to fly above
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:20-21: 'Let the waters swarm with living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth.'

choices.text: Trees, grass, and fruit
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:11, plants come on Day Three — not Day Five.

moonrise.title: The Fifth Day
moonrise.text:
Night has its moon; day has its sun.
What living things fill Day Five?

choices.text: Sea creatures and flying birds
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:20-23: sea creatures and birds fill the waters and skies on Day Five.

choices.text: Cattle and creeping things
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:24-25, cattle and creeping things come on Day Six — not Day Five.

sea_dawn.title: Waters and Skies
sea_dawn.text:
Day Five begins.
Which creatures do you make?

choices.text: Great sea creatures, fish, and every winged bird
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:20-22: God created the great sea creatures and every winged bird, and blessed them.

choices.text: Only bees for the flowers
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:20-21, Day Five brings great sea creatures and every winged bird — not just insects.

sea_creatures.title: Be Fruitful and Multiply
sea_creatures.text:
The seas swarm; birds fly above.
What blessing do you speak over them?

choices.text: 'Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the waters and the earth'
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:22: 'Be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters in the seas, and let birds multiply on the earth.'

choices.text: 'Return to the dust — you have failed'
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:22, God BLESSED the creatures to multiply — He did not destroy them.

bird_flight.title: The Sixth Day
bird_flight.text:
Sea and sky are filled.
What comes on Day Six?

choices.text: Livestock, wild beasts, and creeping things of the earth
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:24-25: cattle, beasts of the earth, and creeping things on Day Six.

choices.text: More stars in the sky
choices.feedback: Stars were made on Day Four. Day Six brings land animals — and humans.

land_creatures.title: In Our Image
land_creatures.text:
The land teems with animals.
What is your final work of creation?

choices.text: Say: 'Let us make man in our image, after our likeness'
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:26: 'Let us make man in our image, after our likeness.'

choices.text: Turn one of the animals into a human
choices.feedback: In Genesis 2:7, God formed man from the dust of the ground — not from an animal.

land_creatures_wind.title: The Crown of Creation
land_creatures_wind.text:
The animals fill the earth.
What is still missing?

choices.text: Declare creation finished — nothing more is needed
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:26, after the animals, God said 'Let us make man in our image.' Creation was not yet complete.

choices.text: A being made in the image of God
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:26-27: humans are made in the image and likeness of God.

among_animals.title: Let Us Make Man
among_animals.text:
No animal bears your image.
How do you make the first man?

choices.text: Transform a lion into a man
choices.feedback: In Genesis 2:7, God formed man from the dust of the ground — not from another creature.

choices.text: Form him from the dust of the ground
choices.feedback: Genesis 2:7: 'The Lord God formed the man of dust from the ground.'

before_man.title: Formed from Dust
before_man.text:
You form a man from the dust of the ground.
How does he become a living being?

choices.text: Speak a word and let him wake on his own
choices.feedback: In Genesis 2:7, God specifically breathed the breath of life into the man's nostrils.

choices.text: Breathe the breath of life into his nostrils
choices.feedback: Genesis 2:7: 'He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and the man became a living creature.'

before_man_lonely.title: The Breath of Life
before_man_lonely.text:
The form of the man lies still in the dust.
What brings him to life?

choices.text: Your breath in his nostrils
choices.feedback: Genesis 2:7: God breathed the breath of life into the man's nostrils, and he became a living being.

choices.text: Water poured over the clay
choices.feedback: In Genesis 2:7, it was God's BREATH — not water — that gave man life.

breath_of_life.title: The Garden
breath_of_life.text:
The man is alive.
Where do you place him?

choices.text: In a desert to prove himself
choices.feedback: In Genesis 2:8, God planted a garden in Eden and placed the man there.

choices.text: In the garden of Eden, to work it and keep it
choices.feedback: Genesis 2:15: 'The Lord God took the man and put him in the garden of Eden to work it and keep it.'

breath_of_life_sacred.title: Eden Prepared
breath_of_life_sacred.text:
The man breathes and lives.
What home do you prepare for him?

choices.text: A garden in Eden, with every tree pleasant to the sight and good for food
choices.feedback: Genesis 2:8-9: God planted a garden in Eden with every tree pleasant to sight and good for food.

choices.text: A field of thorns and thistles
choices.feedback: In Genesis 2:8, Eden was a garden of delight. Thorns and thistles come only after the Fall (Genesis 3:18).

first_garden.title: Behold, Very Good
first_garden.text:
Creation is complete.
What do you say when you look upon it all?

choices.text: 'Behold, it was very good'
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:31: 'God saw everything that he had made, and behold, it was very good.'

choices.text: 'This is a failure — I must start over'
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:31, God saw that everything He had made was very good — not a failure.

first_garden_wonder.title: The Sixth Day is Complete
first_garden_wonder.text:
Man walks in the garden. Creation is finished.
What do you declare?

choices.text: 'Behold, it is very good'
choices.feedback: Genesis 1:31: 'And God saw everything that he had made, and behold, it was very good.'

choices.text: 'I will need to redo the humans tomorrow'
choices.feedback: In Genesis 1:31, God declared everything He had made — including humans — very good.

very_good.title: The Seventh Day
very_good.text:
Six days of creation are complete.
What do you do on the seventh day?

choices.text: Rest, and bless the seventh day, making it holy
choices.feedback: Genesis 2:2-3: 'On the seventh day God finished his work... He blessed the seventh day and made it holy.'

rest.title: The Sabbath
rest.text:
You rest from all your work.
You bless the seventh day and make it holy.

'Thus the heavens and the earth were finished.' (Genesis 2:1)

rest_blessed.title: The Sabbath
rest_blessed.text:
You rest, and bless the seventh day as holy.
All creation is finished — and it is very good.
